_provenance.notes: The Pebble Mine controversy is the most consequential ongoing fisheries policy battle in Alaska history. The proposed copper-gold mine sits in the headwaters of the Nushagak and Kvichak rivers — the two most productive salmon rivers in Bristol Bay and the world. The EPA under Section 404(c) of the Clean Water Act has the authority to veto the Corps of Engineers permit for Pebble. In 2023, the Biden EPA issued a Final Determination restricting Pebble's discharge permits, effectively blocking the mine. Pebble LP has appealed. The status as of 2024 is that the mine cannot proceed under current EPA restrictions. This is considered the most important water/salmon conservation decision in US history.

mine_overview.proposed_location: Upper Nushagak and Kvichak River watersheds, Southwest Alaska
mine_overview.nearest_community: Iliamna, AK (pop. ~116); King Salmon, AK (60 miles)
mine_overview.proposed_mine_life_years: 20+ years of mining, with potential for 100+ year operation if fully developed
mine_overview.proposed_permit: USACE Section 404 Dredge and Fill permit required for wetland impacts

epa_assessment_findings.report_title: An Assessment of Potential Mining Impacts on Salmon Ecosystems of Bristol Bay, Alaska
epa_assessment_findings.key_finding: The proposed Pebble mine could result in the permanent loss of 90+ miles of salmon spawning and rearing habitat in the Nushagak and Kvichak watersheds

regulatory_timeline.event: Northern Dynasty Minerals begins exploration drilling in upper Bristol Bay watershed
Pebble Limited Partnership (Anglo American + Northern Dynasty) formed
Ballot Measure 4 (Alaska Clean Water Initiative) fails — mine opposition mobilizes
EPA begins Bristol Bay Watershed Assessment under Section 404(c) authority
EPA releases Bristol Bay Watershed Assessment: 90 miles of habitat at risk
Anglo American withdraws from Pebble LP partnership — citing project risks
EPA under Trump administration withdraws 2014 proposed determination — process starts over
USACE begins EIS process for Pebble Mine permit
USACE releases Final EIS — recommends against issuing permit based on fisheries impact
Released FBI recordings: Pebble CEO Tom Collier caught on tape downplaying mine size. Collier resigns.
Biden EPA proposes Final Determination restricting Pebble discharge — effectively vetoing the mine
EPA issues FINAL DETERMINATION: vetoes Pebble Mine under Clean Water Act Section 404(c). First use of CWA 404(c) to prospectively restrict a mine before permit issued.
Pebble LP appeals Final Determination in federal court. Case pending. Mine cannot proceed under current legal status.

opposition_coalition.alaska_native_tribes: All 31 federally recognized tribes in the Bristol Bay region formally oppose Pebble Mine
opposition_coalition.commercial_fishing_industry: United Bristol Bay drift and set net fishermen formally oppose
opposition_coalition.sport_fishing: Multiple major sport fishing organizations oppose
opposition_coalition.military: Both of Alaska's US senators, Alaska governor (bi-partisan opposition in some periods)
opposition_coalition.scientific_community: Overwhelming opposition from fisheries scientists and ecologists

economic_comparison.analysis_note: While the mine's one-time mineral value is large, the fisheries provide permanent renewable employment and food security. The EPA assessment concluded the fisheries risk is not justified by any mine benefit given the irreversible nature of the habitat damage.
